Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

UDC 629'12'018'5 : 628*975 : 535'65 



IS : 9421 - 1980 




Indian Standard 

COLOURS OF 
INDICATOR LIGHTS FOR SHIPBOARD USE 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope — Specifies the colours of indicator lights for installations on board ships and on control 
panels and instruments. 

1.1 It does not apply to colours for navigation lamps. 

2. Colours and Their Meaning 

2.1 Indicator lamp colours shall be used with the meanings shown in Table 1. Examples of 
application are also given in Table 1. 

2.1.1 The significance of lamp shall not depend on the interpretation of its colour only. Name- 
plates or engraved strip shall be used as supplementary Information. 

2.1.2 The choice of the number of colours and the use of flashing and steady lights depends on 
the extent and nature of the alarm and signalling system. Generally, flashing lights shall be 
used to indicate situations requiring immediate action, 

2.2 The meaning of these colours is in conformity with 15:9457-1980 'Code of practice for 
safety colours and safety signs \ The colours chosen shall be distinct from each other.

( Clause 2.1 )
